inheritedFrom.note: Core was the probe and went first. The audit METHOD, the pattern set, the status-record shape and the CLA/DCO decision are core's; this repository instantiates them rather than inventing a second judgement, LINKS the trademark policy rather than forking it, and records its divergences in each script's header. A second secret scanner is a second thing to keep correct, and the half nobody re-reads is the half that reports clean.

summary: Every agent-runnable item on the checklist is done and, where it is a property of the tree rather than of one moment, gated as a ctest. The two IRREVERSIBLE steps — the git filter-repo history rewrite and the visibility flip — are prepared, proven, and left for a human to execute together at flip time. No tasklist performs either, and this record exists partly so that no future one can claim it did. This repository is also a SUBMODULE, pinned by the superproject and by each engine repo, which makes the rewrite's blast radius wider here than it was for core.

items.checklistItem: Backend extraction is a hard wall. No generator/pipeline code reachable from an open repo.
items.evidence: docs/pre-open-audit.md §2.3 — the dependency audit is closed across FOUR surfaces, not deny-listed: JS (68 bare specifiers across 16 files against an EMPTY declared set — there is no package.json, so every one is a finding a human classified), Rust (3 dependencies across 3 manifests, every registry crate on `allowedCrates`), C (724 #includes across 133 files, zero of which resolve outside the repository), and the BUILD itself (19 files, zero fetches in CMakeLists.txt or cmake/**). Before US-2 the strings naming the closed backend and web repositories appeared nowhere in the tracked tree. Enforced by scripts/check-open-boundary.mjs, run by the `open_boundary` ctest.
items.notes: The fourth surface is this repository's addition to core's method. A dependency the build DOWNLOADS is one no import graph can see — and libinsimul is layer zero, so what it compiles must be what is committed.

No secret, API key, token, private key, closed pack, committed build output or binary artifact has ever been committed here. items.notes: OPEN_SOURCE_STRATEGY.md marks this item blocked on resolving Trealla's license (GitHub's API says NOASSERTION). The block was LIFTED before this tasklist ran: Trealla is SPDX MIT, resolved 2026-08-12 by reading vendor/trealla/LICENSE at the pinned commit and comparing it mechanically to the SPDX reference body — docs/TREALLA_LICENSE_FINDING.md. The NOTICE is written against that finding, not against a claim, and the gate now checks each stanza's pin against the ONE location the BUILD reads that pin from, so an attribution can never name a different drop than the bytes compiled. One real defect fixed here: rust/Cargo.toml declared `license = "MIT"` while LICENSE is Apache-2.0.

The policy is authored once, in the contract repository, and reached from README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/pre-open-audit.md §3. scripts/check-attribution.mjs enforces BOTH halves: `missing-policy-link` fails if a file this record claims links the policy does not, and `forked-policy` fails if a TRADEMARK.md ever appears in this tree.
items.notes: This repository is not the spec — the conformance corpus here is a vendored MIRROR of core's, so a certification claim is about core's contract version, not about libinsimul. Forking the policy would make the mark mean two different things the first time either copy was edited.

items.checklistItem: Execute the prepared git filter-repo rewrite (the second half of the History scrub item).
items.evidence: scripts/history-scrub.sh (plan-only by default), scripts/history-scrub.replacements.txt and scripts/history-scrub.paths.txt. The plan purges nothing because the audit found nothing to purge, and the script REFUSES --execute in that state rather than rewrite every commit id for no reason. It also refuses a stale report and a non-bare repository, and omits --invert-paths entirely when the paths file is empty (filter-repo reads an empty paths file as `delete the whole tree across all of history`). The machinery is exercised anyway: check D of the `history_scan` ctest runs a REAL filter-repo over a throwaway repository with a planted key and rescans it clean.

items.notes: There is no undo. A repository that has been public for one minute has been cloned, cached and indexed; making it private again removes the link, not the copies. Clear the open items below first, and note that this repository is sequenced in the SECOND wave, after core.

openItems.summary: src/engine_swipl.c and cmake/swipl.cmake can build libinsimul against SWI-Prolog instead of Trealla (-DINSIMUL_ENGINE=swipl). No SWI byte is committed here — it is LOCATED, not vendored — the default build is Trealla, and decision D20 answered the spike NO (docs/SWIPL_MEASUREMENT.md). So nothing is redistributed and no obligation attaches today. But SWI-Prolog's licensing is not a single identifier, and a distributed artifact built with that flag is a different license conversation from every stanza in NOTICE §1. NOTICE §2 records SPDX NOASSERTION rather than guessing.
openItems.owner: Insimul maintainers — read the license text at the pin in scripts/build_swipl.sh and resolve it BEFORE any artifact built with -DINSIMUL_ENGINE=swipl is distributed

openItems.summary: The Prolog standard library embedded in every libinsimul artifact is BSD-2-Clause, and its clause 2 asks that the notice be reproduced in the documentation or other materials provided with the distribution. Shipping the binary alone does not discharge it. NOTICE §5.2 discharges it HERE — but every engine plugin (Godot, Unity, Unreal, the browser package) and every game that redistributes a libinsimul artifact inherits the same duty, and those repositories' third-party notices have not been checked against this list. This obligation exists today, independently of the flip.
openItems.owner: Insimul maintainers — audit each engine plugin's third-party notices against NOTICE §1 before the next plugin release

openItems.summary: Two URLs in this tree name a public repository that does not exist yet, and the project's own documents are not consistent about the names. The trademark policy is linked as https://github.com/insimul/core/blob/main/TRADEMARK.md — the repository core's own policy and status record call themselves — while core's package.json declares its git repository as github.com/insimul/runtime with core at packages/core. rust/Cargo.toml declares repository = https://github.com/insimul/insimul-native. Nothing can verify any of them while the repositories are private, and a link that 404s in a public README is the first thing a reader hits.
openItems.owner: Insimul maintainers — confirm the public repository names at flip time and correct the policy link and the Cargo repository field together

contributorAgreement.decidedBy: 241-pre-open-core US-3; adopted unchanged by 242-pre-open-native US-3, recorded for maintainer review at flip time
contributorAgreement.rationale: Apache-2.0 already grants inbound what the project needs outbound: §5 makes a contribution licensed under the same terms as the work, patent grant included, which is the reason Apache-2.0 was chosen over MIT in the first place. A CLA buys exactly one thing beyond that — the right to relicense contributions unilaterally — and this project's commercial position is the closed generation backend, not the ability to relicense the engine substrate. A CLA is also a documented adoption tax on precisely the people this repository opens for: implementers writing or porting a runtime against a C ABI. And a DCO is enforceable mechanically by a CI check, whereas a CLA needs a bot and a legal record somebody has to operate. Adopting core's decision unchanged is itself part of the reasoning: a contributor working across the contract repository and the native core should not discover that the two ask for different things.
contributorAgreement.consequences: Relicensing insimul-native later would require every contributor's consent. That is the price of the decision, stated rather than discovered.
contributorAgreement.revisitIf: The project wants to relicense or commercially dual-license the native core; or a contributor's employer requires a signed agreement, which is handled per-contribution rather than by making everyone sign one.

trademarkPolicy.rationale: The policy is about the CONTRACT — the conformance corpus, the predicate schema, and the version a certification names are all core's. This repository vendors a mirror of that corpus and implements against it, so it is one of the things the mark is claimed over, not the place the claim is defined. Five copies of a trademark policy is five policies, and the first time one of them is edited the mark means five different things.
trademarkPolicy.enforcement: scripts/check-attribution.mjs: `missing-policy-link` fails if any file listed above stops containing the URL; `forked-policy` fails if a TRADEMARK.md (or a docs/trademark*.md) ever appears in the tracked set. Both are exercised against synthetic positives in tests/attribution_selftest.mjs and against the real tree in tests/run_attribution.sh check D.
trademarkPolicy.cannotCheck: That the linked document still says what this repository believes it says. The link is verified as a string, and core's copy can change underneath it. That is the cost of not forking, and it is the cheaper cost — a stale link is visible to any reader, a divergent fork is not.
